parsed.faithful: The number of birds in this country is immense; nor are those of the carnivorous kind at all deficient. Great numbers of eagles, vultures, hawks, and others of that kind, are met with, and come punctually every year after the tropical rains have ceased. They feed at first upon the flesh-fish which are met with in great quantities on the edges of the defects, where they had lived in the fall springs; but, being forced from their natural habitats when the springs were filled by the rains, who afterwards left to perish on dry land. When these fail, their next resource is from the carcases of the large animals, such as the elephant and rhinoceros, which are killed in the first country by the hunters. Their next supply is the multitude of rats and field-mice which infest the country after harvest. The vast slaughter of cattle made by the Abyssinian armies, the multitude of persons killed, whose bodies are allowed to rot on the field of battle, &c. furnish them with another resource.
